Shields was our first man home, and in finishing 29th did very well, as also did R.

The 4 x 880 Yards was a good race up to the end of the third stage, for Frank Webb on the first leg put us with them, then Fred Ford ran very well in giving us the lead, which Reg.

Some fine running was seen in the 880 yards heats, and Tom Scrimshaw ran well in winning the first heat in 1 min. 58 3-5 sec. from the scratch mark. In the final, however, Frank Tame set a lively pace, but was caught at the dressing room by R.

This race was held from "The Green Man," Putney Heath, and resulted in a win for our old friends, Epsom Harriers. Our team failed to distinguish itself, although running quite soundly, and was led home by R.
Kealey, but Kealey had his reward for some consistent sprinting throughout the season in winning the 220 yards title. Alf Kench retained his 440 yards championship in a close finish with R.
Wilton Dawe ran a clever race to beat R.

We hope to fare well in the four remaining events and repeat our win of last year in the League. The men to represent us were: 3 miles, Ring (4); Carter (7); Allum (10); Ginty (11): and 440 yards, R.
Scrimshaw competing, and off the 7 yds. mark he scored a good win, with R.
Botwright, another of our promising Junior sprinters, second; and R.
Saunders, a promising Junior, was second with R.

The time was on the slow side but the track gave no assistance whatever; being very loose and, indeed, rather dangerous for sprinters, especially near the starting holes. A good field lined up for the 880 Yards and they kept well together until 300 yards to go, when R.
Powell, our new A.A.A. champion, was running for the L.A.C. in the 880 yards race, and he beat R.
To use his own words, "he felt definitely off form." A very poor field turned out for the 440 Yds. and the holder R.
Botwright made good use of his liberal mark to win, with Eddie Pack doing inside 50 seconds to gain second place. R.

Alby Bird was an easy winner of the 880 yards in what was rather slow time, but here we lacked a second runner and so lost a chance of picking up useful points. The 1 Mile saw the two Belgrave men, R.
